rationale: Clinical cases and a cohort describe visual hallucinations without assessing dried fig. The cohort measured incident hallucinations and their association with fatigue, separate from episode frequency. The fig allergy case and the mixed fig-and-olive trial supply no visual episode outcome.

The dietary baseline graphic shows a near-zero positive turkey association with general tremor. Protein and tryptophan studies measured broader motor responses, and a Parkinson camptocormia case describes slight resting tremor without recording diet. Baked turkey and rest tremor direction remain unresolved.

Fresh-date extract increased hot-plate latency in a diabetic-rat study and the tail-flick contrast was inconclusive. Clinical Parkinson reports describe back pain and off-period pain during procedures or changing medication use. The evidence leaves the effect of dried dates on Parkinson pain severity unresolved.

Animal studies used fruit extract or a bark formulation. Historical Lewy body cases record resting tremor without standardized severity or any fig exposure assessment. Direction for eating raw fig and Parkinson resting tremor remains unresolved.

Clinical imaging and diet cohorts assessed apathy without an isolated dried date comparison. The whole dry Ajwa crossover collected an unpublished mood diary, and the adjunct schizophrenia trial gives composite results. Date animal studies measured movement, nociception or reward-related proxies outside the frozen preparation and endpoint.
